title: Declarative authorization registry — code base plus governed data layers
summary: Operation authorization is declared in a typed code registry (effect class + authority + delegation) with two additive data layers: a governed JSON overlay and plugin-manifest authorizations. Code always wins; data layers cannot weaken reviewed declarations (schema rejects local_only/free and code-owned key collisions are dropped).
reusable_steps: Operation authorization is declared in a typed code registry (effect class + authority + delegation) with two additive data layers: a governed JSON overlay and plugin-manifest authorizations
Code always wins; data layers cannot weaken reviewed declarations (schema rejects local_only/free and code-owned key collisions are dropped)
expected_outcome: Three-layer model: (1) libs/core/foundation/authorization-registry.ts is the reviewed source of truth — EffectClass closed taxonomy, AuthorityRequirement, delegation metadata, exact+prefix declarations, fail-safe undeclared default. (2) knowledge/product/governance/authorization-registry.json is a governed-catalog overlay loaded via defineCatalog, schema-validated, additive-only. (3) plugin manifests may carry an authorizations block, scanned only from activation-allowed managed copies, tagged plugin:<id>, cached by content digest + activation status, errors never cached as empty. Lookup order: code exact → code longest-prefix → data exact → data longest-prefix → fail-safe. Data-layer hardening rules: no local_only, no free authority, code collision dropped with warning, manifest parse errors not cached. Undeclared operations resolve to external_mutation + admission so measurement can watch them before enforcement.
